title: Worth Separation Mapping
opening: A result in one area can feel like a verdict on your worth. This map helps you compare what seems required in different settings and what those beliefs lead you to do.

context.title: Cooking and work
context.description: A person accepts a mistake while cooking with a friend. At work, the person treats a typo as proof of incompetence. The typo may still need correction and the draft may still need sending; that practical responsibility is separate from the belief about worth. The contrast points to a work-specific condition to inspect. It does not explain every work reaction.

practice.instructions: Start with a real situation. Keep practical work or responsibility separate from what you believe you must do or be to count as worthy. Add an area where worth feels less conditional when that comparison helps; you may leave a condition unresolved while you decide what to examine next.
practice.responsibility: What work or responsibility needs attention?
practice.condition: What, if anything, feels required for you to count as worthy here?
practice.effect: What does that expectation lead you to do, avoid, or accept?
practice.next: What question or next action will you follow?
